text:
Mia: Quick RFC follow-up — we still haven't landed the claims-pruning story for service-to-service tokens. Problem: large tokens hurt KV cache hit rates and increase runtime memory churn. Proposal: introduce a configurable prune policy (none|minimal|compact|hashed_origin) and default to compact for internal svc calls.

Oliver: +1 on making it configurable. What does 'compact' keep? my thought: {actor_id, intent, ttl, project_id} — drop origin metadata and verbose metadata. We still need org/project for billing/routing though.

Sara: Dropping origin helps size but breaks some tracing/debugging flows. Could we drop origin but add an ephemeral audit_id claim so ops can query the introspection service when needed?

Noah: Async introspect adds latency. For hot paths we could use a short-lived light token (prune_v=1) that caches introspection results in runtime. Idea: runtime caches audit_id -> origin for 5m.

Liam: Ops concern: if we remove origin by default, anyone oncall will get fewer breadcrumbs. audit_id sounds ok but must be presentable in logs. Also need guardrails so compact mode can't be used across trust boundaries.

Eva: Implementation sketch: authn-service adds header and token claim 'prune_v' plus 'audit_id' when compact hashing used. Service-proxy reads header and sets env SERVICE_AUTH_PRUNE per route. Example config: SERVICE_AUTH_PRUNE=compact for internal/* routes.

Mia: Important: RBAC is downstream — if project_id is pruned, services need to fetch entitlements. We should require that compact keeps project_id/org_id (or an opaque project_hash that services can resolve).

Oliver: Could standardize that compact keeps project_id but hashed_origin removes source IP/instance info. hashed_origin option = origin hashed with rotating key so it's auditable but not verbose.

Sara: Edge case: third-party integrations calling internal endpoints — must force prune=none for external callers. We need routing policy: if caller is external, override prune to none and reject if token lacks full claims.

Noah: Suggest introspection fallback when a required claim is missing: service calls authn.introspect(token) and continues. We should add metrics: auth.introspect.count, auth.introspect.latency, auth.prune.misses.

Liam: Security note from me: hashed_origin requires key rotation policy and HSM access. Security-bot: please ensure we get a KMS-backed rotation plan.

security-bot: Automated note — backward compatibility required. New tokens without prune_v are treated as prune_v=0 (none). Add a migration window and opt-in flag per service.

Eva: Minimal code check in proxy:
```python
prune_v = req.headers.get('x-auth-prune-v')
if prune_v == '1':
    claims = compact_extract(token)
else:
    claims = full_extract(token)
```

Mia: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) Add enum and config to authn-service and service-proxy, 2) Canary compact on 3 internal routes, 3) Collect metrics for cache hit rate / introspect calls, 4) Expand.

Oliver: Will add a short RFC addendum detailing the canonical claim set for each mode and the introspection contract. Also propose an assert in dev env that flags missing audit_id when compact is active.

Sara: Ops checklist: ensure logs include audit_id and a mapping table, update runbooks to call introspect if audit_id present.

Noah: Performance note: runtime cache TTL=5m is a sweet spot. We should run a perf test with token sizes -20%, -40% to quantify KV effects.

Liam: Security ops: I'll draft KMS rotation + policies for hashed_origin. Also add alert when introspect latency > 200ms (auth.introspect.latency.p90).

Mia: Next steps: Oliver to write the addendum, Eva to implement proxy flag, Liam to handle KMS plan, Noah to run perf test. If all good, canary next week. :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: canary scheduled for services: ingest-worker, feature-router on 3133333399.

Mia: Perfect — will follow up with a short meeting invite to sync tomorrow.
